_comment: Recorded cost ratios (anchorHz / benchHz) for the performance gate. Update deliberately, in the same PR as an intentional perf change, and say why in the PR description. Costs are dimensionless: they express 'this benchmark costs N noise-anchor operations', so they stay comparable across machines and CI runner classes.

file-manifest/add-1000-entries.reason: addFile called getSyncFeatureFlags() twice per entry (a localStorage+JSON.parse+env read on every call); for the bench's 1000-add loop that was ~76% of addFile time. Read the flags once into a local. Byte-identical: the two reads were synchronous with no await between them, so they observed equal values.

sm20/review-sequence.reason: reviewM2/reviewM3 replaced structuredClone of the optimizer/matrices (recursive walk of ~57k elements + nested cubes) with hand-written shallow copies (.slice of each mutable array, per-row/per-cell for the number[][][] cubes). ~26x faster, byte-identical output; the commit:false clone is the per-review hot path.

queue/build-500-items.reason: queueScrollBudget.splitReviewBudget (two Math.mins) was replaced by composeSession: three-way weight normalization, documents-anchored session sizing, iterated proportional redistribution of unfillable shares, and largest-remainder apportionment. ~11x the (near-free) baseline cost, still ~0.05us per composition; runs once per session build.

queueScrollOrder/combined-sort-300-items.reason: SuperMemo combined-criterion session sort: hoisted the per-item-invariant score terms (priority + jitterWeight*stableJitter(id), and the topic/item classification) out of the O(n^2) selection loop into precomputed Float64/Uint8 arrays, and lifted the two type-specific proportion terms to once-per-position. stableJitter (a BigInt FNV-1a hash) was the dominant cost, recomputed ~n^2 times for n distinct values. ~38x faster; output byte-identical (verified by differential fuzzing, 17732 checks, 0 mismatches).

neuralQueue/spreading-activation-300-nod.reason: SuperMemo neural-queue spreading-activation pass (Phase 4): TS port of the Rust algorithm, propagating activation over a 300-node seeded tree via concept/inter-element/descendant/sibling links with the monotonicity InsertOrUpdate. Runs only on neural-queue depletion (< 20 remaining); the ~0.9us cost reflects the pure-combine hot path. Wider tolerance because Map operations are GC-sensitive at this timescale.
